descriptionChirho: The noun tsephardea refers exclusively to frogs in the context of the Egyptian plague narrative (Exodus 8) and its recall in Psalm 78:45 and 105:30. All four clusters represent the same zoological referent with mere grammatical variation: definite article (ha-tsepharde'im 'the frogs'), indefinite plural (tsepharde'im 'frogs'), definite singular (ha-tsephardea 'the frog'), and prepositional phrases (ba-tsepharde'im 'with frogs'). Multilingual evidence is uniform: Arabic consistently uses dafadi' (الضفادع), Spanish 'ranas', Korean 개구리, Swahili 'vyura', and Hindi mendak (मेंढक). No semantic differentiation exists across these clusters.
